Figure 1:Schematic overview of ResWAM across (a) predictions, (b) architectures, (c) benefits of residuals, and (d) performance highlights.
(a) Predictions of VLAs, WAMs, and ResWAM.
(b) Architectures of WAMs: video-generation WAMs use a video generation model (VGM);
external-world-model WAMs use a vision-language model (VLM) and separate
world model (WM); ResWAM is built on a VLM with residual and action branches.
V. DiT, A. DiT, and R. DiT denote video, action, and residual Diffusion
Transformers, respectively.
(c) Residual features have higher effective rank and focus on the robot and
manipulated objects.
(d) LIBERO-Plus success versus latency, and RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo average success rates across methods. Here w/ and w/o Robot Pretrain indicate with and without robot pretraining on external robot action datasets prior to downstream training.
